'''''Cyclamen hederifolium''''', '''sowbread''',<ref name="PlantAtlas">{{cite web |title=Sowbread ''Cyclamen hederifolium'' Aiton |website=PlantAtlas |url=https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.50m |access-date=2026-07-18}}</ref> or '''ivy-leaved cyclamen''',<ref name="IUCN"/> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Primulaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to woodland, shrubland, and rocky areas at altitudes of up to 1,200 metres in the Mediterranean region from southern France to western Turkey and on Mediterranean islands. It is also [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] farther north in Europe and in Oregon.<ref name="POWO">{{cite web |title=''Cyclamen hederifolium'' Aiton |website=Plants of the World Online |date=2020-09-02 |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:700730-1 |access-date=2026-07-18}}</ref><ref name="PlantAtlas"/><ref name="Blamey">{{cite book |last1=Blamey |first1=Marjorie |last2=Grey-Wilson |first2=C. |title=The Illustrated Flora of Britain and Northern Europe |publisher=Hodder & Stoughton |publication-place=London |date=1989 |isbn=0-340-40170-2 |pages=298–299}}</ref> This widespread cyclamen species is widely [[ornamental plant|cultivated]] and among the most hardy and vigorous in [[oceanic climate]]s.

==Taxonomy==
Two [[subspecies]] are accepted:<ref name="POWO"/>
*''Cyclamen hederifolium'' subsp. ''hederifolium'' — throughout the range of the species, except as below
*''Cyclamen hederifolium'' subsp. ''crassifolium'' <small>(Hildebr.) Culham, Denney & P.Moore</small> — southern Greece

Another related cyclamen from Crete, formerly known as ''Cyclamen hederifolium'' var. ''confusum'', is now treated as a separate species, ''[[Cyclamen confusum]]''.<ref name="POWO-confusum">{{cite web |title=''Cyclamen confusum'' (Grey-Wilson) Culham, Jope & P.Moore |website=Plants of the World Online |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77099941-1 |access-date=2026-07-18}}</ref>

==Etymology==
The species name ''hederifolium'' comes from the Latin {{Lang|la|hedera}} (ivy) and {{Lang|la|folium}} ([[leaf]]),<ref>{{L&S|hedera}}, {{L&S|folium|ref}}</ref> because of the shape and patterning of the leaves. The [[synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] ''C. neapolitanum'' refers to Naples, where the species grows.

==Description==
''Cyclamen hederifolium'' is a [[tuber]]ous perennial growing up to 30 cm tall that flowers and produces leaves in autumn, grows through the winter, and [[aestivation|aestivates]] through the summer after the seed capsules ripen and open.<ref name="Thorogood">{{cite book |last=Thorogood |first=Chris |title=Field guide to the wild flowers of the western Mediterranean |publisher=Kew publishing Royal Botanic Gardens |publication-place=Richmond |date=2016 |isbn=978-1-84246-616-2 |pages=374–375}}</ref>

===Tuber===
The [[tuber]] is round-flattened and produces roots from the top and sides, leaving the base bare. In some other cyclamens (e.g. ''[[Cyclamen persicum]]''), the roots come from the bottom, leaving the top and sides bare. The tuber becomes larger with age; older specimens commonly become more than {{convert|20|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} across.<ref name="Blamey"/> The leaves and flowers grow from buds on the exposed upper surface of the tuber.

===Leaves===
The leaves are 2.5–8 cm long, variable in shape; depending on the specimen, the leaf shape varies from heart-shaped to long and arrow-shaped, usually with 2–3 angled lobes on each side, resembling the juvenile leaves of [[ivy]] (''Hedera''). They are naturally [[Variegation|variegated]], most commonly with a [[wikt:hastate|hastate]] [[Variegation#Reflective|pattern]] in silver to grey-green and various shades of green. In cultivation, plants have been selected where the leaves can be from all-green to all-silver.

The [[petiole (botany)|petiole]] and [[pedicel (botany)|flower stalk]]s of ''Cyclamen hederifolium'' grow outwards and then up, forming an "elbow". From Latin, 'hederifolium' translates to ivy-like leaves. In the closely related ''[[Cyclamen africanum]]'', the stalks grow up from the tuber without a bend near the base.<ref name="Thorogood"/>

===Flowers===
The flowers are produced from late summer to autumn before the leaves; they have five petals 1.2–2.5 cm long; usually pink, purple, or white with a streaky magenta V-shaped marking on the throat, but sometimes pure white with no markings.<ref name="Thorogood"/> They are self-fertile, producing seed without the need for pollination.<ref name="PlantAtlas"/>

The edges of the petals near the tip of the flower are curved outwards into strong [[auricle (botany)|auricles]]. The [[Style (botany)|style]] protrudes only minimally out of the throat of the flower.<ref name="Thorogood"/> These are not present in some other species, such as ''C. persicum''. The flowers are occasionally fragrant. The shape of the flower varies from long and thin to short and squat.<ref>[http://www.srgc.org.uk/smf/index.php?topic=2893.msg108526#msg108526 post 434]. Cyclamen 2009. Scottish Rock Garden Club Forum.</ref>

File:Cyclamen hederifolium var. confusum.jpg|Short flowers with wide throats

===Fruit===
After the flowers finish, the [[pedicel (botany)|flower stem]] coils tightly, starting at the end, and rests above the tuber.<ref name="Thorogood"/> The [[seed]]s are yellow-brown, held in a round [[capsule (fruit)|pod]], which [[dehiscence (botany)|opens]] by 5–10 flaps at maturity. The seeds are covered in a sweet sticky substance attractive to [[ant]]s,<ref name="Blamey"/> which can disperse the seeds up to several hundred metres.<ref name="PlantAtlas"/>

==Cultivation==
[[File:Tapis de cyclamens 3.jpg|thumb|''Cyclamen hederifolium'' naturalised in Belgium]]
''Cyclamen hederifolium'' is usually listed as the hardiest species of cyclamen. In [[oceanic climate]]s, it self-seeds abundantly and will crowd out less vigorous species such as ''[[Cyclamen coum]]'' if the two are planted together. In cold [[continental climate]]s such as Calgary, Alberta, where ''[[Cyclamen purpurascens]]'' grows well, it may not survive.<ref>[http://www.srgc.org.uk/smf/index.php?topic=3084.msg78360#msg78360 post 20]. Cyclamen kuznetzovii. Scottish Rock Garden Club Forum.</ref> It is hardy to [[hardiness zone|zone]] 6, tolerating temperatures down to -18°C, or lower (to -30°C) if protected by reliable snow cover.<ref name="RHSD">{{cite book |title=New Royal Horticultural Society Dictionary of Gardening |publisher=Macmillan Press |publication-place=London : New York |date=1992 |isbn=1-56159-001-0 |volume=1 |pages=792, 796}}</ref>

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]<ref>{{cite web|title=''Cyclamen hederifolium''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5145/Cyclamen-hederifolium/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|accessdate=2020-04-17}}</ref> (confirmed 2017).<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 22 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 24 January 2018}}</ref>

===Cultivars and cultivar groups===
''C. h.'' subsp. ''hederifolium'' has sometimes been divided into two [[form (botany)|forms]] differentiated by leaf and flower characteristics, forma ''hederifolium'' with pink or purple flowers with darker markings at the base of the petals, and forma ''albiflorum'' with white flowers, sometimes with pale pink throat.<ref name=RHS>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/127874/Cyclamen-hederifolium-var-hederifolium-f-albiflorum/Details | title = ''Cyclamen hederifolium'' var. ''hederifolium'' f. ''albiflorum'' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 5 May 2020}}</ref> These are however not considered botanically distinct by the ''[[Plants of the World Online]]'' (POWO) database, which treats f. ''albiflorum'' as a [[synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]].<ref name="POWO-ssp">{{cite web |title=Cyclamen hederifolium subsp. hederifolium |website=Plants of the World Online |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77229562-1 |access-date=2026-07-18}}</ref> The white-flowered form has won the RHS AGM.<ref name=RHS/>

Another published varietal name ''Cyclamen hederifolium'' var. ''poli'', with long sagittate (arrowhead-shaped) leaves, is listed by the Pacific Bulb Society,{{citation needed|date=July 2026}} but is also treated as a synonym of the type by POWO.<ref name="POWO-ssp"/>

Selected [[cultivar]]s of ''Cyclamen hederifolium'' include:
*''Cyclamen hederifolium'' 'Amaze Me', a cultivar with dark pink flowers, is early blooming.
*''Cyclamen hederifolium'' 'Ruby Glow' has particularly deep all-magenta flowers.<ref>photos from [https://alpineenthusiast.blogspot.com/2008/10/ags-loughborough-autumn-show.html AGS Loughborough Autumn show]. Alpines for the Enthusiast (blog).</ref>
*''Cyclamen hederifolium'' 'Stargazer' has upward-facing flowers.<ref>[http://www.gapphotos.com/imagedetails.asp?imageno=46790 ''Cyclamen hederifolium'' 'Stargazer']. GAP photos.</ref>
